subject: Veridian Dedicated Sizing: narrowband peak patterns & SLA gap analysis
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <veridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Veridian Dedicated sizing kickoff - narrowband usage patterns

Alice — thanks for the call this morning. To move from exploration to a Dedicated proposal we need a couple of concrete data points from your side so we can map to GPU slabs and latency SLOs. Below is what would let us produce a deal-specific headroom and SLA-fit recommendation: 

- Per-request token distribution (p25/p50/p95 tokens) — a CSV is fine (many customers call this "token profile").
- Average requests/sec (RPS) and sustained baseline TPS (tokens/sec).
- Peak burst patterns: typical burst multiplier and duration (e.g., 3x for 10 min every hour).
- 95th and 99th latency SLO targets (example: 95th <150ms, 99th <350ms).
- Target model family / quantization you plan to use (full fp16, 8-bit, 4-bit).
- Any geographic/regulation constraints and expected traffic split by region.

We captured initial notes during the call: narrowband queries (mostly 20-120 tokens), mobile client, periodic global marketing spikes. If you can send the CSV token profile and a short note on peak cadence we’ll run a specific tokens/sec -> GPU slab mapping and return: 

1) recommended committed slab count and suggested burst pool, with estimated 95th latency at baseline and peak;
2) headroom % for safe operating buffer and suggested autoscale/burst behavior;
3) cost/ops tradeoffs for quantization.

I’ll loop Marissa and Ben here to prepare a draft once we get the token profile.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alice Wu <alice@veridian.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@veridian.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Veridian Dedicated sizing kickoff - narrowband usage patterns

Diego — attaching the token profile and short notes. High level:

- Average RPS: 230 requests/sec (app-level), average tokens per request: 52 (p95 115, p50 48).
- Sustained baseline tokens/sec: ~11,960 TPS.
- Predictable daily peaks: x2–x3 for ~8–12 min windows (marketing campaigns), unpredictable short spikes up to x6 for <2 minutes.
- SLOs: 95th percentile <150ms, 99th <350ms for our in-app experience. 95% of traffic is NA, 5% EU.
- Model plan: Llama-family variant, will test an 8-bit quantized variant in pilot; want baseline to support fp16 if needed.
- Legal/procurement: procurement@veridian.ai will need the capacity numbers for budgeting.

Files: veridian-token-profile.csv (attached).

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Wu
Head of Platform Engineering | Veridian.ai

Attachments: veridian-token-profile.csv (CSV, 32KB)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Veridian Dedicated sizing kickoff - narrowband usage patterns

Alice — got the CSV, thanks. Quick read and a preliminary mapping below (we'll iterate with Marissa/Ben for final numbers):

Summary of Veridian inputs- baseline tokens/sec: 11,960 TPS- p95 tokens/request: 115- peak patterns: 2–3x sustained (8–12m), micro-spikes x6 (<2m)- SLOs: 95th <150ms, 99th <350ms

Assumptions used for sizing (prelim)- Model: 70B-like Llama fp16 perf profile as a reference on our runtime- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (80GB-equivalent with opt kernels, no quant): 3,500 TPS sustained per GPU at target latency- Quantized 8-bit gives ~1.8x tokens/sec/GPU uplift

Preliminary slab mapping (baseline -> recommended commit)- Baseline compute need (no headroom): 11,960 / 3,500 ≈ 3.4 GPUs (~1 slab if slab=4 GPUs)- Recommended committed slabs: 2 slabs (8 GPUs) to meet baseline with ~40% headroom for steady-state and short bursts- Suggested burst pool: 1–2 additional slabs to absorb x3 sustained peaks and micro x6 spikes; automatic short-duration burst allocation recommended

Estimated latency fit (at target model/perf profile)- With 2 slabs (8 GPUs) and 40% headroom: predicted 95th ≈ 120–140ms (meets 95th <150ms target)- During sustained x3 peaks without burst pool: 95th may slip to ~260–320ms (99th could exceed 350ms)- With burst pool engaged (add 1 slab): 95th recovers to ~150ms, 99th under 350ms

Tradeoffs and next steps- If you adopt 8-bit quant, we can likely reduce committed slabs to 1 slab (4 GPUs) while preserving latency targets, but burst pool still recommended for marketing campaigns.- Marissa: can you validate the 3,500 TPS per GPU estimate for the 70B-like reference on our runtime? Ben: please propose a quantized slab alternative and cost delta.

Action items
1) Ben/Marissa produce two committed configurations (fp16 baseline and 8-bit baseline) with cost delta and operational notes.
2) I’ll draft a short MA (mutual action) timeline for procurement with the numbers so procurement@veridian.ai can budget.
3) Alice: confirm you’re comfortable with the suggested 40% headroom and burst behavior or tell us acceptable risk.

— Diego
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Wu <alice@veridian.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Veridian Dedicated sizing kickoff - narrowband usage patterns

Short note from infra/ops perspective:

- The 3,500 TPS/GPU baseline is reasonable for the 70B-like fp16 reference if we configure continuous batching and keep avg seq len near your p50 (~48 tokens). That number assumes tuned kernels and a steady mix of streaming and sync requests.
- If Veridian will widely adopt 8-bit quant (we’ve validated internal benchmarks ~8-bit dynamic quant), expect ~1.9–2.1x throughput per GPU. I’d use a conservative 1.9x factor for proposals.
- Slab sizing options: 
  * Option A (fp16 conservative): Commit 2 slabs (8x80GB-equivalent GPUs). Burst pool 2 slabs. Headroom target 40% for marketing peaks.
  * Option B (8-bit quant baseline): Commit 1 slab (4 GPUs). Burst pool 2 slabs. Headroom target 50% because quant can add variance; keep burst pool bigger.

Operational notes:
- Autoscale policy: fast short-burst allocator (sub-minute) + capped preemption to avoid noisy neighbor effects.- Canary plan: start pilot on 1 slab with 8-bit quant for 2 weeks; monitor token-level latencies and tail percentiles, then flip commit based on regression alerts.

I’ll attach a quick cost delta table in the pricing doc; Marissa if you want I can sketch a compute-runbook for the on-call team.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice@veridian.ai>, procurement@veridian.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Veridian sizing proposal (summary) + next steps

Alice / Procurement team — attaching the short proposal and the token-profile we received. Summary of recommended path for VD-2027-084: 

- Pilot phase (30 days): 1 slab (4 GPUs) running 8-bit quant variant. Monitor 95/99 tail with our eval prompts and production token flows.
- Committed production (post-pilot): Option A (fp16 conservative): 2 slabs committed (8 GPUs) + 2-slab burst pool. Option B (quant baseline): 1 slab committed + 2-slab burst pool.
- Headroom target: 40% (fp16) / 50% (8-bit) to cover sustained marketing peaks; burst pool to handle x6 micro-spikes.
- Expected SLA fit: baseline 95th ~120–150ms (meets 95th <150ms); with burst pool engaged peaks should remain within 99th <350ms.

Attachments: veridian-dedicated-sizing-v1.pdf (proposal, PDF, 120KB) — includes cost deltas, expected monthly token budget, and the mutual action plan. veridian-token-profile.csv (original).

Next steps (mutual action plan)
1) Procurement: confirm preferred option (A or B) and target contract date for Q4 budgeting.
2) Veridian engineering: approve pilot start date and provide a short list of eval prompts for tail monitoring.
3) Redwood: schedule pilot kickoff, deliver runbook, and enable burst pool for first 10 business days.

If procurement wants a shortened pricing table or a one-pager we can cut that today. Proposed week for pilot kickoff: Aug 23 — is that workable?

— Diego
